## Goal

Take your standalone Shiny app (Lab 2) and **export** it with the `shinylive` R package so it
runs in the browser, then serve it locally with a plain static server. No R process is needed to
execute the app once exported; the reader's browser does the work via webR.

If you did not finish Lab 2, use the ready-made app at `apps/penguins-app/`.

---

## 1. One-time setup

Make sure the `shinylive` R package is installed (it is on the workshop image; otherwise install it):

```r
install.packages("shinylive")
```

## 2. Export your app

Run R (console in your IDE) from the workshop root, and export your app folder to a `site` folder:

```r
shinylive::export("apps/penguins-app", "site")
```

The two arguments are the **source app folder** and the **destination folder**. `shinylive`
walks the app, decides which R packages it needs, downloads the Shinylive web assets (including
webR / WASM builds of those packages), and writes a fully static site into `site`.

## 3. Serve it locally

A static server just hands out files:

```r
httpuv::runStaticServer("site")
```

Open the printed URL (for example http://127.0.0.1:8008) in a browser. Your Shiny app should
appear and be fully interactive, with **no R server running the app**.

::: {.callout-note}
The first load is slow (seconds): the browser downloads webR and the packages. Reload after the
first load to feel the difference made by the browser cache.
:::

## 4. Inspect the exported site

Open the `site/` folder. You should see the app files plus a large `shinylive/` subfolder with
JavaScript, worker scripts, and `.wasm` binaries. This is the "web assets library" in action: the
host only stores files; the browser runs them.

Use your IDE's file explorer and, if curious, open `site/index.html` to see the bootstrapped page.

## 5. Confirm data stays local (the privacy property)

In the running app, upload the bundled `penguins.csv` (or any other CSV). Open your browser's
**Network** tab (DevTools) and reload. You will see requests for static assets only; the uploaded
file is read into browser memory and never POSTed anywhere.

::: {.callout-warning}
The flip side: open the app's downloaded source in DevTools (Sources tab). Your **code is public**
to anyone with the URL. Never put API keys or passwords in a Shinylive app.
:::

## 6. Stretch: pin dependencies with renv

Reproducible exports pin package versions with renv. The lifecycle is three commands:

```r
renv::init(project = "apps/penguins-app")     # once: discovers deps, writes a renv.lock
renv::snapshot(project = "apps/penguins-app") # capture dependency updates into the lockfile
shinylive::export("apps/penguins-app", "site")
```

`shinylive::export()` reads the lockfile and bundles **exactly those versions** as WASM builds.
(`renv::restore()` is the reverse: it installs the exact versions a lockfile pins.)

---

**You are done with Lab 3.** You now have a serverless Shiny app ready for any static host.
Next, `lab-04-shinylive-quarto.qmd` embeds Shiny directly in a Quarto report.
